text:
maya: Hey team — saw a weird one during an install on WSL2. I ran the quickstart installer (tarball -> install.sh) and ended up with a folder literally named '~/.redwood' (tilde not expanded). localtest/localserve can't find profiles, and auth login is failing after that. Anyone seen literal-tilde writes from the installer?

joel: ouch. can you paste `redwoodctl --version` and `ls -la` output for the parent dir?

maya: redwoodctl version: 0.12.3
Here is the dir listing I saw:```
/opt/apps$ ls -la
drwxr-xr-x  5 root root 4096 Mar  2 10:12 .
drwxr-xr-x 12 root root 4096 Mar  2 09:58 ..
drwxr-xr-x  3 1000 1000 4096 Mar  2 10:12 '~/.redwood'
```

samir: that looks like the installer wrote the literal string. which install command did you run exactly? did you use quotes around ~ or run as sudo?

maya: I grabbed the quickstart and used `sudo ./install.sh --prefix /opt/apps` because I wanted it system-wide. I think that was dumb but I did it.

joel: `sudo` can change HOME, but it shouldn't create a quoted tilde folder. common culprit: the install script uses something like `echo '~/.redwood' > "$prefix/path"` or a `sed` that wasn't allowed to expand the tilde.

samir: quick workaround: move the folder and re-run installer as non-root or expand manually. e.g.```
sudo mv "~/.redwood" "$HOME/.redwood" || sudo mv /opt/apps/'~/.redwood' $HOME/.redwood
chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) $HOME/.redwood
```
That should get you a sane config layout.

maya: moved and adjusted perms, that fixed profile lookup. but now `redwoodctl auth login` opens the browser and the callback returns 400: `redirect_uri_mismatch`. localserve was started with `--port 8085` though.

devex-bot: Known issue #452: install-generated local OAuth client defaults to port 8080; CLI flag for `localserve --port` is not propagated to the saved client redirect URI. Workaround documented.

joel: yeah that matches #452. installer currently writes redirect_uri http://127.0.0.1:8080/callback. If you run localserve on a different port the auth flow fails. two quick fixes: (1) start localserve on 8080 or (2) update the saved client redirect.

samir: to update client redirect manually you can run:```
redwoodctl auth create-client --name local-dev --redirect http://localhost:8085/callback
# or edit $HOME/.redwood/client.json and change redirect_uris to the port you used
```
Note: `auth create-client` will print the client id/secret; you can replace the file the installer created.

maya: ok created a new client and replaced the client file, auth login succeeded. thanks both. I'll open a PR to make the installer expand ~ (and not write literal quotes) and to make the client redirect default match `localserve --port` or accept an env var.

joel: awesome. when you file PR, add a small integration test that runs the tarball install under a noninteractive shell and checks that no path contains a literal tilde. also add a test that `localserve --port` updates the redirect URI or that the installer uses an env var.

samir: I'll assign the issue to you and put the `needs-e2e` label. also cc @devex for tracking.

maya: will do. I'll include repro steps, minimal logs, and the quick fix commands above. tagging @joel for review when ready. :thumbsup:
